lines.st: The last thing the expedition members saw before passing out was two strange people rushing in and holding the enemies off for a moment with unbelievable beams of light.
But the two of them soon seemed to be struggling. It felt like they ought to step in and help, but with nothing in hand but archaeological digging tools, what could they possibly do...
Perhaps because far too much had happened that day, and all of it chaos, the expedition members' overwhelmed minds finally gave out, and they sank into a thick, sticky sleep.

lines.x: The expedition members woke up utterly exhausted. They had only come here wanting to do a bit of out-of-the-ordinary exploring, so why had they ended up seeing so many incomprehensible things?

That greenhorn Casas had claimed he'd gotten his hands on a map, but it turned out to be nothing more than a strange stone tablet that glowed like a flashlight. And yet, wherever the tablet's light pointed, paths that hadn't existed before would appear.
Following its guidance, they found the ruins of a vast ancient civilization where no one had ever set foot—only to be surrounded by all manner of strange creatures and soldiers.
And then Casas, who had eagerly dug up an ancient relic, turned every enemy into a mist of blood in an instant and transformed into a hulking figure in bizarre attire...
It was a total mess—they couldn't make heads or tails of what had happened! If those two hadn't shown up out of nowhere... Well, in any case, they owed them their thanks.
I honestly don't know how to thank you. If you hadn't helped us, we'd definitely have been done for.
Ugh... My head's still kind of foggy, and I can't muster any strength...
You were all out cold for a good half day, so you haven't fully recovered yet. Best find a way to make camp here tonight and head out tomorrow.
But is it safe here? Won't those soldiers from before show up again?
I don't think you have any other choice. After all, not all of your members have woken up yet.
Sigh, fair enough. We'll do as you say.
Lorenz looked at the shattered tablet and disc, which no longer gave off any light, and sighed. They were probably beyond analysis now, but perhaps they still had some other use.
She had seen and analyzed similar creations before, and had deduced that some will was interfering with the Blackflow Forest, molding the Blackflow into “Realtopias” and “Utopias,” one after another.
Even though Lorenz neither knew nor cared about its purpose, she couldn't help wondering what sort of being possessed such technology, and what its technological foundation might be.

This technology's control over information far surpassed that of Theory-4 or Cadejo, yet its user seemed to employ it merely to repeatedly create different quasi-life-forms and ecosystems within the Blackflow Forest.
The trail these expedition members had walked, and indeed the entire “ancient civilization ruins,” were in essence probably aggregates of information—a discarded draft awakened by Casas's wish.
Now that the two Ideal Sources had been destroyed, the “Residents” of this area, and likely the area itself, would gradually dissipate within two or three days.

Until then, it was best to let these expedition members rest properly and set out tomorrow. Having laid eyes on such high-density information entities, being out cold for half a day was getting off lightly.

As for the young man named Casas... after being possessed by an Ideal Source like that, it would be a stroke of luck if he even kept his original self intact. He won't be waking up for two or three days at le—

Ugh, my head hurts... Did I fall asleep?
Don't tell me I got so excited after digging up the treasure that I passed out, haha.
Listen, I had a dream. I dreamed that two rulers of an ancient Bolívar civilization went to war over the right to interpret and worship the sun, and then...
Wait, isn't this... Waaah! Why's my treasure all broken?! I saved up over half a year's living expenses and scholarship money to buy that ancient tablet on the black market!
And this newly excavated one too... It's over. It's all over.
Uh... Why are you all so quiet? Why are you staring at me? Is there something on my face...
You jerk, you've got the nerve to ask us?! You tricked us into coming here for a research project, then suddenly turned into some bizarre freak and beat me up!
I thought I was gonna die! Now you're gonna get a taste of almost being crushed by a giant rock!
Hey, let's talk this out! Don't do this! I surrender, I surrender! But I really don't know what happened! When did I...
Still playing dumb! Take this—Eclipse Tribe Whirlwind Fist Scissor Kick!
Come on, the Eclipse Tribe never had a move like that! Ow!
Are they really going to fight? Should we go break it up?
You didn't do many club activities in college, did you? Some young people are just like that—the more they roughhouse, the closer they get. Let them be.
...Did my father and you roughhouse like that back in the day?
He never told you? Self-proclaimed titles like “Death Incarnate” and “Destroyer of the Earth,” that sort of thing.
What tacky titles. That's not like his taste in names at all.
Ruthless as ever. And you think “Little Theory” Mk. I, II, and III shows such refined taste in naming?
I'd say they're better than the names one of his juniors came up with, like “Shorty” and “Lofty.”
I'll reserve judgment on that for now.
So, what about the person or thing you were looking for? Did you find it?
No. I just picked up some real-time signals of the Blackflow Forest's internal structure being drastically reshaped, so I dragged you along to see if we could find any clues.
Unfortunately, all that's left here are the results of those changes.
Saving lives is a good thing too. But that aside, what on earth were those things? An ancient Bolívar civilization? The Sunlit Tribe and the Eclipse Tribe? Even I've never heard of such things.
There's nothing like that even in Cadejo's information. Such a civilization probably never existed in history at all. Or perhaps it isn't part of Terra's history...
Hey! You two over there, won't you come eat something with us?
Maybe later. Go ahead and eat first.
You students quit horsing around and eat something, or you won't have the energy to get out of here tomorrow.
Stop tickling me, hahahaha, that tickles, hahaha... Have mercy...
Night fell, as if in a hurry to bring these past few days of expedition to a close.
Everyone in the camp let their taut nerves relax, except Lorenz and Payukaka, who still gazed into the distance at the fog that even the searchlights couldn't pierce.

lines.st: The abnormally restarted abandoned Utopia model has stopped responding. Information fragment defragmentation process started...
Source of abnormal reverse-detection intent detected...
Abnormal records uploaded to the storage unit. Requesting next instruction from the core...

lines.x: Too bad. Looks like the transmitter I planted in the information stream awaiting recovery has been disposed of.
